newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian central bank to move 5-10% reserves to ECB. [CORRECTED 00:55 GMT 25/2]
newsitem.headline: Belgian central bank to move 5-10% reserves to ECB. [CORRECTED 00:55 GMT 25/2]

text.p: The Belgian National Bank will transfer between five and 10 percent of its reserves to the European Central Bank once a single currency is launched, Governor Alfons Verplaetse said on Monday.

"We have to contribute between five and 10 percent of our external assets, for which we will receive as counterpart a credit from the European Central Bank," Verplaetse told the central bank's annual shareholder meeting.
At the end of 1996, the Belgian central bank held gold and foreign exchange reserves to the equivalent of 593.1 billion Belgian francs ($17.1 billion or around 15.3 billion Ecus).
(Corrects Belgian francs amount and dollar conversion, Ecu amount already correct).

Under the Maastricht Treaty, central banks participating in economic and monetary union (EMU) will contribute the equivalent of 50 billion Ecus of their reserves to the European Central Bank according to their share in its capital.

Verplaetse reiterated the BNB's shareholders have no claim on external assets, such as gold and foreign exchange reserves, dampening speculation about whether they might receive a share of the assets once monetary union starts.
Separately, Verplaetse repeated he believed the Belgian central bank now had a good balance of gold in its reserves after recent sales.
The BNB is one of Europe's few listed central banks, with half its capital, or 200,000 shares in public hands. Fifty three shareholders, representing some 15,978 shares, attended Monday's meeting.
